newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end sharply down on regional worries.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end sharply down on regional worries.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended sharply lower on Monday as investors retreated to "safe-haven" markets in the region, said analysts.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 leading stocks lost 12.78 points, or 1.19 percent, to 1,060.53, while the small-capitalised Second Board shed 7.01 points, or 1.24 percent, to 559.93.

"The selling has been brought on by regional worries. When people are not sure of the situation in the region, they pull out and go into Singapore," said Chong Yoon Chou, investment manager at Aberdeen Asset Management in Singapore.
Telekom was among the hardest-hit blue chips, falling 50 cents to 11.00 ringgit. The stock has a 10-percent weighting on the Composite Index.
"Foreign hedge funds have been shorting the market," said Christopher Neoh, institutional dealer at BBMB Securities.

A 15-percent devaluation in the Thai baht since last Wednesday and fighting between rival army factions on the streets of Phnom Penh have had a damaging effect on the confidence of regional investors, said analysts.
The release of Malaysia's May trade report showing a 156.8 million ringgit surplus did little to boost morale, they said.
"We are already underweight Malaysia and are now reducing the weighting further to seven percent," said Morgan Stanley in a recent report.
Berjaya Industries was the day's most actively-traded stock, rising nine cents to 3.04 with 41 million shares changing hands.
Analysts said the company's management may be looking to inject new businesses into it after the group's recent restructuring left it without several core businesses, said analysts.
Construction company DKLS was also actively traded. It shed 70 cents to 10.10 ringgit with 4.03 million shares traded. The company has a 60 percent stake in a Cambodian toll-road project.

Cambodia is currently in the midst of a power struggle between its two prime ministers. Factions of the countries army loyal to the two men plunged the capital Phnom Penh's streets into violence over the weekend.
Analysts said the company was more prone to the effects of Cambodia's political instability as it is relatively small compared to other Malaysian companies invested there.

Resorts World shed 50 cents to 7.10 ringgit on speculation that the hotel and resort operator would post significantly lower results for its half-year to June 30 due to be released later in July, said analysts.
Market volume totalled 274 million shares, valued at 1,754 million ringgit. Losers pummelled gainers 479 to 128.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot July contract fell 14.7 points to 1,050.0, August shed 14.7 to 1,054.0, and September lost 16.7 to 1,054.0. Spot July contract volume stood at 554 lots, while August and September each had three lots changing hands.
